name: Advent 2026
description: A 25-question journey through the Christmas story — from ancient prophecy to the birth of Jesus.

questions.text: What is the name of the child mentioned in Isaiah 7:14?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 names the child Immanuel, meaning 'God with us,' signifying God's presence and promise.

questions.text: In Isaiah 9, what promise is given to those walking in darkness?
options: They will see a great light
They will find peace on earth
They will be delivered from enemies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 9:2 states that those walking in darkness will see a great light, symbolizing hope and divine revelation.

questions.text: What action does Isaiah 9:4 say God will do to the oppressors of Israel?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 9:4 states that God will break the yoke of their burden and the bar of their shoulders, symbolizing liberation from oppressors.

questions.text: According to Micah 5:1, who is the ruler's origin described as?
questions.explanation: Micah 5:2 states that the ruler's origin is from Bethlehem Ephrathah, emphasizing the prophecy of a ruler coming from that small town.

questions.text: Who was being addressed in Micah 5:2?
options: Bethlehem Ephrathah, a small clan among the clans of Judah
questions.explanation: This is stated in Micah 5:2, where God speaks directly to Bethlehem Ephrathah saying "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah...."

questions.text: What does the opening of Matthew 1 primarily focus on?
options: The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
questions.explanation: Matthew 1 begins with the genealogy of Jesus, tracing his lineage from Abraham to David and through generations, establishing his royal and Jewish heritage (Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.text: What is significant about the lineage listed in Matthew 1:1–17?
options: It emphasizes Jesus' royal and legal descent
It shows Jesus' connection to pagan nations
It focuses on Jesus' spiritual talents
questions.explanation: Matthew's genealogy emphasizes Jesus' royal and legal descent through Joseph, highlighting his royal Davidic lineage (Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.text: What is the main purpose of Matthew 1's genealogy?
options: To establish Jesus' legal and royal lineage
questions.explanation: The genealogy in Matthew 1 aims to establish Jesus' legal right to the throne of David, confirming his messianic credentials (Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.text: Where was Jesus born according to Luke 2?
questions.explanation: Luke 2:4-7 describes Jesus being born in Bethlehem, the city of David, because Joseph was of the house and lineage of David.

questions.text: Why did Isaiah tell Ahaz not to ask for a sign from the Lord?
options: Because God did not want to reveal Himself
Because trusting God was the sign
questions.explanation: Verse 11 shows Isaiah urging Ahaz to ask for a sign, but God tells him not to test the Lord. Isaiah emphasizes that trusting God's promise itself is the sign.

questions.text: What is the purpose of Luke's Gospel as stated in Luke 1:1-4?
options: To give an orderly account so readers may know the certainty
questions.explanation: Luke writes so that Theophilus may know the certainty of the teachings he received (Luke 1:4).

questions.text: Which priest's division is mentioned in Luke 1:5?
questions.explanation: Zechariah belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, as mentioned in Luke 1:5.

questions.text: What was Zechariah's initial response to the angel's message about his future son?
questions.explanation: Zechariah doubted the angel's words because of his and his wife’s old age (Luke 1:18).

questions.text: In Luke 2, what sign did the angels give the shepherds?
options: A baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger
questions.explanation: Luke 2:12 gives this sign to the shepherds.

questions.text: Who were the first to hear the announcement of Jesus' birth from the angels?
questions.explanation: Luke 2:8-9 describes shepherds tending their flocks who are visited by angels announcing the birth of Jesus.

questions.text: What phrase did the angel use to describe Jesus' arrival?
options: A Savior, who is Christ the Lord
questions.explanation: Luke 2:11 records the angel proclaiming Jesus as 'a Savior, who is Christ the Lord,' highlighting His divine role.

questions.text: According to Luke 2, what was Mary’s reaction after the shepherds visited her?
options: She told everyone in the town
questions.explanation: Luke 2:18-19 describes Mary pondering all these things in her heart after hearing and seeing the shepherds' report.

questions.text: What was the main purpose of the wise men’s visit?
options: To offer gifts and worship Jesus
To deliver a message from the king
questions.explanation: The wise men came to worship Jesus and offer gifts, as stated in verses 10-11.

questions.text: What was Herod’s plan after learning about the child?
questions.explanation: Herod secretly plotted to kill Jesus to eliminate any threat to his throne (verses 13-16).

questions.text: Where did Joseph, Mary, and Jesus go after fleeing Herod?
questions.explanation: Joseph was warned in a dream to escape to Egypt with Mary and Jesus, fulfilling prophecy (verse 13-15).

questions.text: Does Matthew state the monetary value of the wise men’s gifts?
options: No, the value is not stated
Yes, it gives an exact number
Yes, it lists the market price
Yes, it gives the value in denarii
questions.explanation: Matthew lists the gifts, but does not state a monetary value.

questions.text: What prophecy did Matthew say was fulfilled by Jesus’ return from Egypt?
options: Out of Egypt I called My Son
questions.explanation: Matthew quotes Hosea 11:1 to show Jesus' return from Egypt fulfilled this prophecy (verse 15).

questions.text: In John 1:1, what does the verse say about the Word?
options: The Word was with God, and the Word was God
The Word was created by angels
The Word was only a prophet
The Word was a song in the temple
questions.explanation: John 1:1 states the Word was with God and was God.

questions.text: According to John 1, what was the Word’s relationship to God?
options: The Word is a messenger from God
The Word was with God and is God
The Word was created by God
The Word is simply a teaching
questions.explanation: John 1:1 states that 'The Word was with God, and the Word was God,' affirming the divine nature of the Word.

questions.text: What is the significance of Jesus being called 'the Word' in John 1?
options: He reveals God’s nature and will
questions.explanation: Referring to Jesus as 'the Word' signifies that He reveals God's very nature and communicates God's will to the world, as mentioned throughout John 1.
